title: `sudo pyenv` and `sudo nvm` do not work, though SPEC.md says a new Python or Node version needs `sudo`
foundBy: session agent, while comparing how each /opt toolchain adds a version for SBX-111
details:
SPEC.md §3.1 says the toolchains under /opt are read-only for the dev user, so a new language version needs `sudo`. As the sandbox user, `sudo pyenv --version` prints `sudo: pyenv: command not found`. Fedora's sudo replaces PATH with its `secure_path`, which does not name /opt/pyenv/bin, and it drops PYENV_ROOT. `sudo nvm` cannot work at all, because nvm is a shell function that ~/.bashrc sources.

Reproduce in ghcr.io/codesweep-ai/sandbox:v0.0.0-20260929195333-38b6867ec3dd as a user with the image's NOPASSWD sudo.

A user who follows the rule meets a failure that names nothing about /opt. A fix either makes sudo find the tools, for example with a sudoers drop-in that extends `secure_path` and keeps PYENV_ROOT and NVM_DIR, or documents the commands that work.
